issues.detail: Error handling is thin: the fetch calls in onMount and the mutator have no response.ok checks or failure paths, and the SSR/test guidance is a single prose sentence with no code.

scenarios.name: conditional-search-fetcher
scenarios.rationale: Both create a fetcher store with a computed key that returns null below 3 characters and explain that a null key part skips the fetch. B scores higher because it URL-encodes inside the computed key, as the rubric asks, and it explicitly describes the idle state. A encodes inside the fetcher instead, which is less aligned with the rubric, and it mentions idle only loosely.

scenarios.name: astro-shared-persistent-cart
scenarios.rationale: Both use persistentMap, a computed count, Number/String conversion, and useStore from the React and Vue packages, with the store in one module and plain-function actions. B adds removal, cross-tab detail and gotchas, and a more complete Vue island; A is concise and states the strings note more explicitly in a comment, but both only note it in code comments.

scenarios.name: store-testing-and-mutation-invalidate
scenarios.rationale: B covers every rubric item: createMutatorStore with invalidate('/api/projects'), keepMount to trigger onMount, cleanStores in afterEach, and get() only in tests/actions. A uses createMutatorStore and invalidate correctly but never mentions keepMount (it uses listen/allTasks instead) and says nothing about restricting get() to tests and actions.
